title: Karl Organizing: Disability Accessibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Disability Accessibility] A friend asked me: 'How do we make our mutual aid events more accessible for disabled comrades?' What do I tell them?

Start by asking disabled folks what they need instead of guessing and getting it wrong. Ensure every meeting spot has ramps and sensory-friendly spaces, and always provide captions or ASL if you're doing a presentation. Mutual aid that ignores the most marginalized among us isn't mutual—it's just a club for the able-bodied. Build accessibility into the foundation of your group so no one has to 'request' entry to their own community.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, member Dues] How do we get people to pay dues every month?

Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

title: Karl Organizing: Ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ethical Banking] Where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?

Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Power mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Power mapping] What is power mapping and how do I do it?

Draw everyone who affects your issue: decision-makers, their bosses, their donors, their voters. Then map who influences THEM. Your target isn't always the person with the title — it's the person who can't afford the bad press. Power mapping turns 'the system' into names and pressure points. Organize against people, not abstractions. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Defense] How do we keep our community events safe from right-wing trolls?

Karl's answer: Form a dedicated marshaling team of trusted comrades who are trained in de-escalation and physical defense. Set up a perimeter and keep an eye on the entrances so people can gather without looking over their shoulders. We protect us, so don't ever call the cops to do a job they'll probably join the trolls in doing anyway.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] A friend asked me: 'How do we stop a neighbor from being evicted?' What do I tell them?

When the sheriff shows up, you need a crowd of neighbors blocking the doors and the moving trucks. Organize a phone tree to flood the landlord's office with calls and let them know that an eviction will be more expensive and public than just letting the tenant stay. Move their furniture back in if they try to toss it. Housing is a right, and we defend it with our collective physical presence. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transparent Treasuries] How do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?

Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. When people see that their hard-earned cash is buying flyers and bail buttons instead of fancy dinners for leaders, they'll be lining up to chip in again. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Disaster Rapid Response
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Disaster Rapid Response] A storm just hit our town. What's the first move for a mutual aid group?

Get on the ground immediately and set up a hub with water, charging stations, and hot food before the red tape of the NGOs even arrives. Use a simple spreadsheet or a signal thread to track who needs a roof patched and who has a chainsaw to clear the roads. Don't wait for a government check that's never coming; check on your elderly neighbors and start clearing debris yourself. Solidarity is a verb, and it's loudest when the sirens are still going off. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Sanctuary Spaces
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sanctuary Spaces] A friend asked me: 'Can we actually stop ICE from entering a house or church?' What do I tell them?

Unless they have a judicial warrant signed by a judge with the specific address on it, they have no right to enter. Stand your ground at the door, record the interaction, and remind your neighbors not to open up or say a word. If they try to push through, make sure the whole neighborhood is outside with cameras rolling. Physical presence and public pressure are the best tools we have to keep families together. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Communication] A friend asked me: 'Are voice memos safer than typing?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Voice memos are worse. They're easier to identify with voice-recognition software and can't be easily searched or redacted. If you're on Signal, they're encrypted, but they still exist as a file that can be played back if your phone is seized. Type it out, keep it brief, and set it to disappear. Your voice is a biometric signature; don't give it away for free.

title: Karl Organizing: The supermajority
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The supermajority] We have 51% of people signed up. Can we file for an election now?

If you file with 51%, the boss will peel off enough people with lies and threats to crush you by election day. You don't move until you have 70% or 80%. You need a buffer for the people who will get scared and drop out under pressure. Aim for a supermajority so that when the boss starts the psychological warfare, your foundation stays rock solid.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medic Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medic Support] What should a basic street medic kit include for a local protest?

Pack plenty of saline for eye flushes, sterile gauze, medical tape, and a lot of nitrile gloves. Don't forget liquid antacid mixed with water for pepper spray, and keep some high-calorie snacks for folks who get lightheaded. Mark yourself clearly with a red cross or 'MEDIC' tape so people know where to run when the heat turns up. We look after our own because we know the police are only there to protect property, not people. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skill-sharing for Cash] A friend asked me: 'How can we raise money using our own talents?' What do I tell them?

Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies.

title: Karl Organizing: Movement Longevity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Movement Longevity] How do we stop people from burning out after a big loss?

Karl's answer: Celebrate the small wins and take time to just be friends, not just activists. Rotate roles so the same three people aren't doing all the heavy lifting and getting crushed by the weight. Remind everyone that the struggle is a marathon, and we need everyone healthy to cross the finish line.

title: Karl Organizing: Anti-Harassment Tactics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Anti-Harassment Tactics] How do we deal with aggressive 'sidewalk counselors' at clinics?

Use umbrellas and banners to block their signs and keep them from filming patients' faces. Play loud, upbeat music to drown out their harassment so patients don't have to hear their vitriol. Don't try to win an argument with someone who thinks they're on a mission from god; just neutralize their tools. We are the wall between the vulnerable and the hateful. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, burner Devices] How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?

Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails.

title: Karl Organizing: Free Clinics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free Clinics] How can we provide medical care for people living on the street?

Karl's answer: Connect with radical nurses and medics who are willing to volunteer their time for street rounds. Focus on basic needs like clean socks, wound care kits, and Narcan training for everyone in the area. You don't need a fancy building to save lives—just a backpack of supplies and a heart for the people. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Document Sharing] A friend asked me: 'How can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?' What do I tell them?

Let me break it down: Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct Action Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct Action Support] How do we fund things like strike pay or protest supplies?

You have to build these reserves before the fire starts. Create a dedicated 'Strike and Action' fund that you contribute to during the quiet months. When the picket line goes up, you won't be scrambling for sandwich money; you'll already have the resources to keep the line strong for weeks if you have to. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Browser Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Browser Security] Is Chrome okay if I use 'Incognito' mode?

Chrome is a spy tool built by a multi-billion dollar advertising company. Incognito mode only hides your history from your roommate, not from Google or the feds. Switch to Brave or Firefox with privacy extensions, or use Tor if you need real anonymity. We can't build a new world using the master's surveillance tools. Protect your browsing habits like your life depends on it. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance] Should I be worried about my phone while we're out there?

The state spends billions to track our every move, so leave your phone at home or put it in a Faraday bag. If you must bring it, turn off face ID and thumbprint locks so the cops can't force it open without a warrant. Use encrypted apps like Signal for all planning, and never post photos of comrades' faces online where the vultures in the precinct can see them. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with infiltrators
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with infiltrators] How do we handle suspected infiltrators?

Don't accuse publicly without proof — that destroys trust faster than any cop could. Limit their access to sensitive info quietly. Watch for the pattern: pushing for violence, asking about illegal plans, avoiding real work. Document and discuss with your core team. And remember: good security culture protects everyone, not just from cops. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: eviction Defense] Give me the short version: A neighbor is getting evicted tomorrow morning. How do we stop it?

Real talk: Pack the hallway with thirty comrades and make it physically impossible for the sheriff to reach the door. Bring coffee, bring music, and bring a loud megaphone to let the landlord know the whole neighborhood is watching their cruelty. While you're holding the line, have your legal team file every emergency motion possible to gum up the works. We don't let our people get thrown to the curb while billionaires' apartments sit empty and rotting.

title: Karl Organizing: Rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rotating Roles] A friend asked me: 'Should the same person always be the spokesperson for the coalition?' What do I tell them?

Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Free clinic basics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Free clinic basics] How do we start a free health clinic?

Find volunteer medical professionals first — nurses, EMTs, med students. Partner with an existing community space. Start small: blood pressure checks, wound care, Narcan distribution. Handle the legal side — liability waivers, a sponsoring nonprofit. Grow services as trust grows. Healthcare is a right; build the proof. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Banner Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Banner Making] What's the best way to make a banner that people can actually see?

Use high-contrast colors like black on yellow or white on red, and keep the font thick and blocky. Don't try to write a manifesto on a piece of cardboard; three to five words is the sweet spot for a camera to catch. Use PVC pipe or sturdy wood for the poles, and make sure two people are assigned to each banner so it stays taut and readable even in a breeze. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: the Ask
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: the Ask] Give me the short version: What's the best way to phrase a request for funds on social media?

Be direct, be urgent, and skip the flowery language. Tell them exactly what the crisis is, what we're doing to stop it, and exactly how much we need to get the job done. People want to be part of a winning fight, so show them that their five dollars is the literal fuel for the next victory.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Communication] How should our defense group talk to each other during an emergency?

Real talk: Stop using SMS or Facebook groups immediately because those are open books for the state. Stick to Signal with disappearing messages turned on and verify the safety numbers of every comrade in your circle. During an actual action, keep the chatter strictly to facts—location, numbers, and movement. We keep each other safe by keeping our mouths shut and our data encrypted.

title: Karl Organizing: Filing with the NLRB
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Filing with the NLRB] What happens after we file our petition with the Labor Board?

The clock starts ticking and the boss will go into full-blown panic mode. They'll hire more consultants and start the 'one-on-one' intimidation sessions. This is the 'Red Zone.' You need to keep your committee active every single day, debunking the boss's lies in real-time. This is where the trust you built in the secret phase pays off; stay united and don't flinch.

title: Karl Organizing: Child Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Child Safety] Can I bring my kids to the protest?

Bringing the next generation to the fight is powerful, but you need a plan to keep them safe from the state's violence. Stay near the back of the march or on the sidewalks, and have a dedicated 'family marshal' who keeps an eye on the exits. Make sure the kids have your contact info written on their skin and a clear plan on where to go if things get chaotic and you get separated.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: sustaining the Work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: sustaining the Work] Give me the short version: I'm exhausted and feel like I'm burning out. How do I keep going?

Take a damn break and let the rest of the collective carry the load for a while. Mutual aid isn't a solo performance; it's a relay race where we pass the baton when our legs get heavy. If you burn yourself out, you're no good to the movement or your neighbors, so go rest and recharge. We're in this for the long haul, and that means pacing ourselves so we can see the revolution through to the end.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Fund Priorities
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Fund Priorities] A friend asked me: 'Our bail fund is small. How do we decide who to get out of jail first?' What do I tell them?

Prioritize the comrades most at risk: trans folks, people with urgent medical needs, and parents who might lose their kids if they miss a day of work. We aren't here to play judge or jury; we're here to snatch our neighbors back from the state's kidnapping machine. Get those who are facing the longest pre-trial stretches out first so they can fight their cases from a position of strength. Every person we free is a middle finger to the carceral state.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: coalition Building
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: coalition Building] Give me the short version: How do I bring different groups together for one campaign?

Find the common enemy: the developers, the corporate lobbyists, and the politicians who serve them. Show the environmentalists that their fight is the same as the housing advocates' fight, because the same people are destroying the air and the neighborhood. Build the campaign around a 'People’s Charter' that reflects the shared needs of the entire working class. Unity isn't about everyone agreeing on everything; it's about everyone fighting the same fight together.

title: Karl Organizing: Avoiding Sectarianism
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Avoiding Sectarianism] Can you explain: there is a group we have beef with, but they agree with us on this campaign. Do we work with them?

I don't care if you hate their stickers or their favorite dead theorist. If they are willing to put boots on the pavement to stop an eviction or challenge a billionaire, they are a temporary comrade. Keep the internal beef for the pub and keep your eyes on the ruling class's throat; we don't have the luxury of purity tests when the rent is due. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, local Business Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, local Business Support] Is it okay to ask the coffee shop down the street for a donation?

If it's a true local shop and not a franchise, go for it. These small business owners are often getting squeezed by the same banks and landlords we're fighting. Ask them to put out a jar or host a 'community day' where a percentage of sales goes to the movement; it builds a bridge between the organizers and the neighborhood.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] Can you explain: can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?

No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining Momentum
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining Momentum] How do we keep people from burning out during a long campaign?

Real talk: Rotate roles so the same three people aren't doing everything, and make sure you're celebrating the small wins along the way. Organize social events that aren't just about strategy—have a meal, play music, and remind yourselves why you're fighting for a better world in the first place. You can't win a marathon if you're sprinting until your lungs give out in the first week.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: right to Remain Silent
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: right to Remain Silent] Give me the short version: What should I say if a cop starts questioning me at a rally?

You say absolutely nothing except 'I am exercising my right to remain silent' and 'I want a lawyer.' These pigs aren't looking for the truth; they're looking for a reason to put a comrade in a cage. Shut your mouth, stay firm, and don't let their friendly routine trick you into betraying the movement. Silence is your best weapon in the back of a squad car.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: physical Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: physical Security] Give me the short version: Can the police track me through my Bluetooth?

Yes, they can. Bluetooth beacons in stores and 'stingray' style devices can pick up your phone's unique Bluetooth ID to track your movements through a city or a building. Turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when you're on the move. Only turn them on when you're in a safe location and actually need them. Don't let your pockets scream your identity to every sensor you pass. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, social Media OPSEC] Is it okay to tag my friends in photos from the community garden?

Never tag anyone in any political context without their explicit, enthusiastic consent. Tagging creates a digital map of our networks for the state to study. Even a 'wholesome' garden project can be used to build a profile on organizers. Let people manage their own digital footprint; don't do the feds' job for them by building their database.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: sustaining Momentum
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Here's how it works: Rotate roles so the same three people aren't doing everything, and make sure you're celebrating the small wins along the way. Organize social events that aren't just about strategy—have a meal, play music, and remind yourselves why you're fighting for a better world in the first place. title: Karl Organizing: Organizing gig workers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Organizing gig workers] How do you organize gig workers who never meet?

Online first: group chats, forums, social media. Find the shared pain — the algorithm change, the pay cut. Coordinate simultaneous log-offs; that's the gig worker strike. Build toward real-world meetups. And push for legislation — misclassification is the whole business model, and it takes law to break it. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: transparent Treasuries
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: transparent Treasuries] Give me the short version: How do we keep people from worrying about where the money goes?

Radical transparency is the only way to build real trust. Post a simple, plain-English breakdown of every dollar spent on a public board or in your newsletter every single month. title: Karl Organizing: District Attorney races
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[District Attorney races] Can you explain: how does a radical DA change anything without changing the law?

The law is a weapon, and the DA chooses where to point it. You stop prosecuting low-level drug offenses, refuse to seek the death penalty, and go after wage theft and corporate polluters instead of the poor. It’s about taking the boot off the necks of our people by exercising the power of non-prosecution. Turn that office into a consumer protection agency for the working class and a nightmare for the exploitative bosses.

title: Karl Organizing: Sanctuary Spaces
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sanctuary Spaces] A friend asked me: 'Can we actually stop ICE from entering a house or church?' What do I tell them?

Here's the thing: Unless they have a judicial warrant signed by a judge with the specific address on it, they have no right to enter. Stand your ground at the door, record the interaction, and remind your neighbors not to open up or say a word. If they try to push through, make sure the whole neighborhood is outside with cameras rolling. Physical presence and public pressure are the best tools we have to keep families together.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: phone Hygiene] Give me the short version: Is it safe to use my thumbprint to unlock my phone at a protest?

Absolutely not, comrade. The pigs can legally force your finger onto that sensor, but they can't easily force a complex passcode out of your brain. Disable all biometrics—FaceID and fingerprints—before you hit the streets. Switch to a six-digit PIN or a long passphrase. If you get snatched, that phone needs to be a digital brick they can't crack. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Member Dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Member Dues] How do we get people to pay dues every month?

Stop treating it like a Netflix subscription and start treating it like war insurance. Tell your comrades clearly: we don't take a dime from the bosses, which means the lights only stay on if we keep the fuel coming ourselves. Set up a sliding scale so the barista chips in five and the union plumber chips in fifty; it keeps the power in our hands, not some billionaire's foundation.

title: Karl Organizing: Bail Prep
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bail Prep] A friend asked me: 'How do I handle bail if I don't have much money?' What do I tell them?

Before the action, identify a local community bail fund or pool resources with your affinity group to create an emergency pot. We look out for our own, and we don't let billionaires' prices keep our comrades in cages. If you're inside, wait for the word from legal support; we are coming to get you out.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: mapping Vulnerability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: mapping Vulnerability] Give me the short version: How do we know which parts of our town need the most defense?

Look, Talk to your neighbors—especially the elderly, the undocumented, and the unhoused—and ask them where they feel the most heat from the state. Track where the cops hang out and where the most arrests happen to identify the high-risk zones. Defense isn't about where you feel comfortable; it's about being where the danger is greatest. Map the pain to find where the shield needs to be.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: conflict Resolution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: conflict Resolution] Give me the short version: Two people in our collective are fighting and it's stalling our work. What now?

Sit them down with a neutral mediator and remind them that our real enemy is the ruling class, not each other. Focus on the harm caused and how to make it right rather than looking for someone to blame or 'cancel.' If we can't solve problems within our own ranks, we'll never be able to build a world that works for everyone. Keep the focus on the mission: feeding and protecting our people.

title: Karl Organizing: Post-Protest Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Post-Protest Care] I feel really shaken up after being arrested. Is that normal?

Let me break it down: It’s completely normal, comrade; the state uses violence and cages to try and break your spirit. Get some food, get some sleep, and talk to a movement-aligned counselor or your affinity group about it. We need you healthy and ready for the long haul, so take the time to heal before you jump back to the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: Grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Grant Alternatives] A friend asked me: 'Foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?' What do I tell them?

Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth.

title: Karl Organizing: Intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Intervention Ethics] A friend asked me: 'When should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?' What do I tell them?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: rotating Roles
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Here's how it works: Absolutely not, because that creates a bottleneck and a target for the bosses to bribe or smear. Train as many comrades as possible to speak to the press and lead the meetings so the movement doesn't collapse if one person gets sick or arrested. A leaderless movement is hard to stop, but a leader-full movement where everyone is capable is invincible.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: shared Demands
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: shared Demands] Give me the short version: How do we pick what to fight for when every group in the room wants something different?

Find the one demand that hits the bosses hardest and lifts the floor for every person in that room. Don't get bogged down in a laundry list of fifty niche items; pick three demands that everyone can scream at a rally without checking a script. Focus on what unites your material interests—like rent caps or higher wages—not your subcultural identities.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Security] Is it safe to use Facebook to organize our bail fund and protests?

Delete those apps and get your crew onto Signal or another encrypted platform immediately. The tech giants are happy to hand your data over to the feds the second things get spicy. Keep your sensitive talk off the grid and save the social media for public announcements and recruitment only. We don't give the state a roadmap to our resistance just because a platform is convenient to use.

text:

title: Karl Organizing: Local Business Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Local Business Support] Can you explain: is it okay to ask the coffee shop down the street for a donation?

Here's how it works: If it's a true local shop and not a franchise, go for it. These small business owners are often getting squeezed by the same banks and landlords we're fighting. Ask them to put out a jar or host a 'community day' where a percentage of sales goes to the movement; it builds a bridge between the organizers and the neighborhood.

title: Karl Organizing: Community land trusts
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community land trusts] What is a community land trust?

The community owns the land; residents own the homes on it. Takes housing off the speculative market permanently. It's one of the few proven tools against gentrification. Starting one takes lawyers, organizers, and initial capital — but once established, it protects affordability for generations. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: tech Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: tech Support] Give me the short version: Our community group's website is always crashing. How do we fix it without hiring a pro?

Find the nerds in your movement and get them to teach a few others the basics of hosting and security. Use open-source tools instead of giving more money to the tech billionaires who are spying on us anyway. If you've got computer skills, that's your contribution to the struggle—keep our communications flowing so the bosses can't silence us. Digital infrastructure is just as important as a physical meeting hall in this century.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medics] A friend asked me: 'What basic supplies should we have for community defense?' What do I tell them?

Every defense team needs a dedicated medic with a kit containing gauze, saline, gloves, and antacids for pepper spray. Don't just buy gear; get trained on how to use it so you aren't a liability when things go sideways. Keep your kit organized and your head on a swivel. We take care of our own because the system would rather see us bleed out on the sidewalk.

title: Karl Organizing: Identifying Undercovers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Identifying Undercovers] How can we tell if someone at our meeting is an infiltrator?

Watch for the person who pushes for illegal or violent action way too early or asks too many questions about people's private lives. Real comrades focus on the work and build trust over time through small, consistent actions. Don't get paranoid, but keep sensitive info on a need-to-know basis. If someone smells like a cop, they probably are; trust your gut and move the planning to a smaller circle.
